payload.rationale: I estimate a 60% chance of a Denver win. No current team evidence is supplied, so this is a modest-confidence background judgment rather than a game-specific forecast. Assuming Denver is the home team, as the matchup ordering suggests, home-field advantage supports a probability above 50%. Older performance context also modestly favors Denver: its 2024 team performed substantially better than Jacksonville's, though transferring that difference to September 2026 requires substantial discounting. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that Jacksonville may have improved more since then, or Denver may have important quarterback or roster absences. The strongest reason it could be too low is that Denver may retain a substantial underlying team-quality advantage compounded by playing at home. I treat ties and fair-value settlements as excluded outcomes, not Denver losses, consistent with the stated binary-scoring rules.
limitations: No current research or outside evidence records were supplied.
No verified 2026 roster, injury, quarterback, coaching, recent-performance, rest, or weather information is available.
Denver home-field status is inferred from matchup ordering rather than independently confirmed.
Historical team strength is an uncertain guide after substantial roster and coaching turnover.
The estimate concerns the binary win outcome; excluded settlement outcomes are not separately estimated.
